description: One weather reading during one shift. THE TABLE SHIPS EMPTY IN v0.19.3 AND THAT IS THE POINT — its shape is what the compliance-event snapshot fields denormalise from and what the Heat Exposure Event's maxima will be computed over, so fixing it now means v0.19.4 wires a fetch rather than migrating a schema under live records. v0.19.4 ports the Open-Meteo service already running in farm_app, walks every shift with no end_datetime every fifteen minutes, and backfills closed shifts from the archive API so a shift that ran before the service was switched on can still be documented.

fields.description: The instant these conditions were true. Not the instant they were fetched — a backfilled reading from the archive API is a true statement about 14:15 last July whenever it was written, and conflating the two would make every backfilled shift look like it was documented after the fact.
fields.label: At

fields.description: Air temperature. What a person quotes, and not what Oregon's heat rule turns on — see heat_index_f.
fields.label: Temp (°F)

fields.description: THE NUMBER THE RULE ACTUALLY USES. OAR 437-004-1131 engages at a heat index of 80 °F and adds obligations at 90 °F, and heat index is temperature and humidity together — 88 °F at 70% humidity is a 100 °F heat index and a shift somebody could be cited over while the thermometer reads comfortably.
fields.label: Heat Index (°F)

fields.description: Relative humidity. Kept alongside the derived heat index rather than only the result, so a disputed index can be recomputed from what was actually observed.
fields.label: Humidity (%)

fields.description: Wind speed. The spray shift's equivalent of heat index: nearly every pesticide label sets a maximum, and it is the first thing an Oregon Department of Agriculture drift investigation asks for.
fields.label: Wind (mph)

fields.description: Wind direction in degrees. Direction is what turns a speed into a statement about where the spray went and which neighbouring property was downwind.
fields.label: Wind Direction (°)

fields.description: Precipitation over the interval. Rain during a harvest shift is a food-safety fact under the Produce Safety Rule before it is a productivity one.
fields.label: Precipitation (mm)

fields.description: Where the number came from: 'Open-Meteo forecast API', 'Open-Meteo archive API', 'on-site station', 'foreman reading'. An auditor is entitled to know whether a temperature was measured at the block or modelled for the grid square, and a column that did not say would invite the question at the worst moment.
fields.label: Source

fields.description: When this row was written. Together with reading_datetime it is what distinguishes a live fifteen-minute fetch from an archive backfill, honestly, on the face of the row.
fields.label: Fetched

name: Farm Shift Weather Reading
